t: Concatenated Divisibility — Bitmask DP with Greedy Reconstruction
o: We must order up to 13 numbers so their decimal concatenation is divisible by k, returning the lexicographically smallest valid ordering. Concatenating `x` after a prefix with remainder `r` yields remainder `(r * 10^len(x) + x) % k`, so divisibility only depends on the subset used so far and the running remainder mod k. With n ≤ 13 and k ≤ 100 there are at most 8192 × 100 states — tiny. Example 3 shows some inputs have no answer, so feasibility must be checked before greedily building the result.
k: State = (subset mask, remainder mod k); transition appends one number
Backward feasibility DP lets us greedily pick the smallest next number
Only 10^len mod k matters, precompute pow10 per number

a.i: Define f(mask, r) = true if the numbers outside `mask` can be appended (in some order) to a prefix with remainder `r` to reach remainder 0. This is computed top-down with memoization. Once feasibility is known, walk forward: at each step try unused numbers in ascending numeric order and take the first whose resulting state remains feasible. This greedy is correct because fixing smaller earlier elements always dominates lexicographic order regardless of later choices.
s: Precompute len[i] and p10[i] = 10^len[i] mod k.
Memoized f(mask, r): try every unused i, recurse on (mask|bit, (r*p10[i]+nums[i])%k); base case mask==full returns r==0.
Otherwise greedily append the smallest unused i keeping f true.
a.t: O(2^n · n · k) time — each of 2^n·k states tries n transitions; memo table dominates space at O(2^n · k).
a.sp: O(2^n · k) for the memoization table plus O(n) recursion depth.

w: Use the bitmask DP approach directly — it is the intended solution and simple enough to explain. Pitfalls: forgetting the empty-list case (Example 3), using 64-bit arithmetic for remainders (values up to ~10^5 with 13 digits exceed 32 bits conceptually, though mod keeps things small), and sorting candidates by value (not index) during reconstruction. Follow-ups: largest valid permutation, counting valid permutations, or k up to 10^9 (then use hash maps for remainder states).
